title: Money tools in your language
description: Understand saving, home loans and take-home pay in Australia. Five simple calculators, clear examples and explanations in your language.
intro: Choose a question. Try your numbers. Understand the result.
chooseTool: What would you like to work out?
toolIntro: See how your savings and interest could grow together.
See what an offset balance or extra payments could change.
Find a monthly savings amount for your target.
Set aside money for essential bills if income stops.
See the estimated amount paid into your bank account.
local: Free to use. Your numbers stay in this browser.
scope: These five calculators and explanations are available in this language. Bank product terms, detailed guides and other pages are currently in English.
advanced: More detail on the English calculator
rateHint: Example rate, not a bank offer. Enter a rate you have checked.
expensesHint: Include rent or repayments, food, bills, transport and minimum debt payments.
superIncluded: Does this amount include employer super?
superNo: No — employer super is on top
superYes: Yes — it is my total package
helpDebt: I have a HELP / student loan debt
threshold: I claim the tax-free threshold with this employer
salaryScope: 2026–27 estimate for Australian tax residents with a TFN and standard Medicare treatment. Assumes ordinary earnings and 12% employer super, subject to the cap. Excludes salary sacrifice and other deductions. This is payroll withholding, not your final tax return.
oldYear: These payroll rules are for 2026–27. Check the current ATO rules before using an estimate for another year.
afterYears: Saving period (years): {years} · before tax and fees
noContribution: Add monthly savings to estimate a timeframe.
super: Employer super (paid to your super fund)
error: Check your entries. Use numbers within the limits shown; an empty field is not zero.
savingsNote: Assumes an unchanged rate, interest added monthly and deposits at month-end. Weekly and fortnightly savings are converted to a monthly average. No withdrawals, tax, fees or inflation. Actual bank calculations and bonus conditions can differ.
mortgageNote: Principal-and-interest loan with monthly repayments and an unchanged rate. The regular repayment is based on the loan without an offset. A constant 100% offset reduces the balance charged interest. Extra repayments are added each month. Excludes fees, redraw and lender-specific rules.
goalNote: Assumes an unchanged rate, monthly compounding and deposits at month-end. No withdrawals, tax, fees or inflation. For a home deposit, add a separate allowance for buying costs to your target.
emergencyNote: Target equals essential monthly expenses multiplied by the months you choose. Time to reach it is rounded up to full months. Interest and inflation are excluded. The example is not a recommended buffer size.
lessonTitle: One idea that makes money easier
lessonIntro: Compound interest means your interest can earn interest too.
lessonDetails: Imagine a fixed 10% yearly rate. This is a teaching example, not a bank offer.
The first $10 is interest on your $100.
Now interest is calculated on $110: $11 more. Of that, $1 is interest earned on the earlier interest.
lessonNote: No new deposits, tax or fees. This example compounds yearly; the calculator above compounds monthly.
contact: Report a problem with a translation
disclaimer: Educational estimates, not personal financial advice. Check current rates, eligibility and fees with the provider.
translationNote: Language changes the explanation, not the Australian rules or currency. Translations are prepared with AI assistance. Tell us if wording is unclear.
languageBasis: We prioritise widely used community languages in Australia, using the ABS 2021 Census language-at-home results. Mandarin, Arabic, Vietnamese, Cantonese and Punjabi lead the non-English list. Written Chinese is offered in simplified and traditional forms; these are writing systems, not a one-to-one mapping to spoken languages. Spanish and Korean are additional community options. This is not a ranking of nationalities. 2026 Census results are due from June 2027.
